I don't have any agenda here; I am just totally curious. With all of the back-and-forth I'm seeing in the world and on the internet, with the "fatpeoplehate" side and the "body positive" side (that's an oversimplification, I know, but still...), I just wondered – for you, personally, when is a person not just overweight, but fat? I just get the sense that there might be varying answers and I'd like to see them. Thanks!
When you are overweight for your body type and it's not due to muscle.
When somebody is overweight and it isn't from muscle mass.

From a purely biological perspective, it comes down to the percentage of white adipose tissue you have. There are ways to accurately measure this, but the simplest metric tends to be waist-to-height ratio. The health profession has defined cut-offs, but I'm uncertain how arbitrary these are (there certainly isn't some massive change in your health by losing or gaining a gram - it's on a continuum). There are correlations between weight and certain health issues, and these could be (and likely are) used to create some form of meaningful definition, but I sense that largely (outside of the health profession) the definition is cultural.

From Wikipedia :

The degree to which a person is overweight is generally described by body mass index (BMI). Overweight is defined as a BMI of 25 or more, thus it includes pre-obesity defined as a BMI between 25 and 30 and obesity as defined by a BMI of 30 or more. (source)

Fat is BMI 25 and over unless a body builder, and body builder is defined as a person with low body fat whose overdeveloped muscles push them into the overweight category, generally considered to be gym-rats or "swole", not the delusional couch potato who thinks he's muscular but never gets more exercise than opening the fridge. Swole people work very hard at developing their muscles, they are easy to identify just by using your eyeballs. If someone has to tell you how much muscle he has, he's not muscular. Examples of body builders are Dwayne Johnson (The Rock) and [a younger] Arnold Schwarzenegger.

Fat is also under 25 BMI but with a high body fat percentage. Ideal body fat percentage for men is 2-15% and for women is 10-20%.

So, there are people who are clinically of a healthy weight but are over-fat and therefore fat. Some overweight people are clinically overweight (or obese) but have a low percentage of body fat and therefore are not fat. BMI skews in favor of more fat people being labeled as healthy than healthy people being labeled as overweight. Swole folks are the only legitimate outliers, and they are not fat, therefore BMI is a good measure in general, but body fat percentage is the best measure to determine fatness.
